acceptance: A boot refresh that re-execs with ResumeWaves=k arms a handoff the next image takes as k (red today: 0)
fix: Before the boot refresh's exec, re-arm the handoff with cfg.ResumeWaves (same pid survives exec), so the next image resumes at the same wave.
routed_reason: console dispatchability audit 2026-10-01: a fix must change go/internal/loopchain/ (protected surface); cfg.ResumeWaves at process start comes only from takeReexecHandoff (cmd_loop_chain.go) reading loopchain.TakeHandoff's Claim/attempt marker; the boot-refresh exec path (cmd_loop_boot_refresh.go's defaultBootRefreshExec, same-PID syscall.Exec) has no way to arm that marker because the writer, Refresher.recordAttempt, is unexported and reachable only through a full Refresher.Refresh() cycle (ahead-check/rebuild/repin) the boot self-heal path doesn't run, so a correct fix needs a new exported arm primitive inside internal/loopchain; the item's declared files (cmd_loop_prebatch.go, cmd_loop.go) don't even name the real call site (cmd_loop_boot_refresh.go). Confirmed unfixed on main.
summary: PR #712 takes the wave handoff once in runLoop and carries it in loopConfig.ResumeWaves. The boot refresh runs later, per batch (cmd_loop_prebatch.go); if HEAD moves in the seconds after a boundary rebuild and the boot refresh re-execs, the new image finds no handoff and restarts at wave 0 with the full budget (logged). Rare: at a wave boundary lanes are idle and sync-main already ran.
title: A boot refresh that re-execs right after a boundary re-exec loses the wave resume point
